title: Metaphysics II: modality, causation, laws, time and free will
audience: a college student in a philosophy degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Study the metaphysics of how things could be and why they happen: possible worlds (modal realism, ersatzism and fictionalism), essence and de re modality, dispositions and powers, causation (regularity, counterfactual and process theories), laws of nature (Humean and non-Humean), time (the A-theory and the B-theory, presentism, eternalism and the growing block, and time travel) and free will (compatibilism, libertarianism and skepticism).
primary_reading: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (free): entries on possible worlds, causation, laws of nature, time and free will

weeks.1: Modality: necessity, possibility and possible worlds
weeks.6: Problems for counterfactual theories: preemption and overdetermination
weeks.8: Laws of nature: Humean and non-Humean views
weeks.9: Time: McTaggart, the A-theory and the B-theory
weeks.10: Presentism, eternalism, the growing block and time travel
weeks.11: Free will: the consequence argument and compatibilism
weeks.12: Libertarianism, Frankfurt cases and free will skepticism

blocks.deliverable: Evaluate the incredulous stare objection to modal realism.
Compare a modal and a definitional account of essence.
Analyze a preemption case with a counterfactual theory.
Week 7 midterm; compare the best-system account with a governing view of laws.
Reconstruct McTaggart's argument and one reply.
Write a three-page essay on the consequence argument.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Metaphysics paper: write a 2,500-word paper on one debate (modal realism, the counterfactual theory of causation, Humean laws, presentism or the consequence argument) that states the strongest argument on each side, uses at least one case or thought experiment of your own, and defends a conclusion.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
